when_to_use: Standard starting baseline for any tabular classification or regression problem with structured numerical/categorical columns.
tradeoffs: Extremely fast training and low memory usage via histogram-based binning; slightly more prone to overfitting on tiny datasets (<1000 rows) compared to simple linear models or small Random Forests.
common_pitfalls: Setting num_leaves too high causing rapid overfitting; not specifying categorical_feature for category columns.

when_to_use: High-accuracy gradient boosting baseline, particularly strong when tuning max_depth and subsample/colsample_bytree.
tradeoffs: Exact greedy split finding can be slower than LightGBM on large datasets unless tree_method='hist' is used.
common_pitfalls: Default hyperparameters can overfit without early stopping or regularizing gamma, reg_alpha, and reg_lambda.

when_to_use: Datasets with many high-cardinality categorical features or default hyperparameter settings where minimal tuning time is available.
tradeoffs: Symmetric (oblivious) trees offer robust generalization and fast CPU inference, but training on high-dimensional sparse data can be slow.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to pass cat_features indices or strings; using one-hot encoding prior to CatBoost which negates its native target statistics handling.

when_to_use: High-cardinality categorical columns (e.g. zip codes, city IDs, category codes) where one-hot encoding would blow up feature dimensionality.
tradeoffs: Compresses high-cardinality categories into a single informative numeric feature; severe risk of target leakage if not strictly computed out-of-fold.
common_pitfalls: Target leakage caused by calculating target statistics across the entire dataset before splitting CV folds. Must always use Out-of-Fold calculation and add smoothing/additive prior.

when_to_use: Pairs of domain-related continuous measurements (e.g., debt/income, area/rooms, price/quantity).
tradeoffs: Helps tree models capture non-linear relationships and interactions without needing deep trees; combinatorial explosion if applied blindly to all pairs.
common_pitfalls: Division by zero resulting in Inf/NaN values without proper epsilon clipping or replacement.

when_to_use: Medium-to-high cardinality categorical features where category frequency/rarity carries independent predictive signal.
tradeoffs: Simple, robust, zero risk of target leakage; treats different rare categories with identical counts as equivalent.
common_pitfalls: Overwriting the original category without keeping both the categorical ID and the frequency count.

when_to_use: Hierarchical or multi-entity tabular datasets where entities are nested inside groups (e.g., customer transactions within store ID).
tradeoffs: Provides rich contextual statistics (mean, std, min, max, count) relative to peer group; introduces NaNs for single-member groups.
common_pitfalls: Computing group aggregates on test sets separately from training sets, or leaking future temporal data in time-series settings.

when_to_use: Standard CV strategy for classification tasks to guarantee identical class label proportions across all folds.
tradeoffs: Provides variance-reduced, unbiased out-of-fold validation scores; not applicable when samples are grouped or temporally ordered.
common_pitfalls: Using standard unstratified KFold for imbalanced classification which leads to high fold score variance.

when_to_use: Whenever multiple rows belong to the same underlying entity, patient, user, or device (indicated by a group_id column).
tradeoffs: Prevents identity leakage across train and validation folds; fold sizes may be slightly unbalanced depending on group sizes.
common_pitfalls: Splitting randomly across rows instead of groups, leading to severely over-optimistic CV scores that fail to generalize on the leaderboard.

when_to_use: Temporal data where predictions are required on future time steps (e.g. stock, demand forecasting).
tradeoffs: Strictly prevents lookahead leakage; training folds have variable or reduced historical sample sizes.
common_pitfalls: Randomly shuffling rows across time, which leaks future information into past predictions.

when_to_use: Ensembling predictions from multiple distinct model architectures (e.g. LightGBM + XGBoost + CatBoost) when evaluating ranking metrics (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC).
tradeoffs: Immune to model probability calibration differences; cannot be used when exact calibrated probabilities or absolute loss metrics (log_loss, MSE) are required.
common_pitfalls: Applying rank averaging when the competition evaluation metric is Log Loss or Root Mean Squared Error.

when_to_use: Combining predictions of several strong base models using a meta-learner (e.g. Ridge / Logistic Regression / small LightGBM).
tradeoffs: Usually achieves higher performance than any single model; increases pipeline complexity and inference latency.
common_pitfalls: Training meta-models on train-set predictions instead of strictly out-of-fold cross-validated predictions, leading to massive second-stage leakage.

when_to_use: Ensembling probabilities or regression outputs where weights are optimized via Nelder-Mead or grid search on out-of-fold predictions.
tradeoffs: Simple, highly effective, interpretable model contributions; requires well-calibrated predictions from each component model.
common_pitfalls: Optimizing blend weights on the test set instead of strictly cross-validated OOF predictions.

when_to_use: Handling NaNs appropriately depending on model family: native handling for GBDTs, explicit median/indicator for linear models.
tradeoffs: Native GBDT handling preserves missingness as an informative split direction; linear models crash on NaNs.
common_pitfalls: Reflexively replacing NaNs with 0 or mean before GBDT training, which removes the tree's ability to branch on NaN status.

when_to_use: Selecting categorical representation based on cardinality and model family.
tradeoffs: Native category dtype in LightGBM/CatBoost avoids memory explosion; one-hot encoding is only suitable for low-cardinality categoricals (<10 unique values) in linear models.
common_pitfalls: One-hot encoding columns with thousands of levels, consuming excessive RAM and causing GBDT split fragmentation.

technique_name: Feature Selection via Permutation Importance / SHAP
when_to_use: Pruning noisy, redundant, or uninformative features after generating extensive interaction candidates.
tradeoffs: Reduces overfitting and speeds up training; computing SHAP values or permutation tests on large datasets can be computationally intensive.
common_pitfalls: Using default GBDT feature_importances_ (split gain), which heavily biases toward high-cardinality continuous features.

when_to_use: Whenever cross-validation score diverges significantly from training score (overfitting).
tradeoffs: Increases bias slightly while substantially decreasing prediction variance across folds.
common_pitfalls: Tuning learning rate without simultaneously tuning n_estimators and early_stopping_rounds.

when_to_use: Variables with heavy non-linear step functions (e.g. age brackets, tax brackets).
tradeoffs: Transforms continuous data into categorical buckets; loses granular rank ordering within bins.
common_pitfalls: Choosing arbitrary bin edges instead of quantiles (pd.qcut) or domain-informed boundaries.

when_to_use: Cyclical periodic features such as hour of day (0-23), day of week (0-6), or month (1-12).
tradeoffs: Preserves circular distance (e.g. 23:00 is adjacent to 00:00); generates two correlated features per original column.
common_pitfalls: Treating cyclical values as pure linear continuous features without cyclic projection.

when_to_use: Regression targets with extreme right skewness (e.g. monetary values, house prices, counts).
tradeoffs: Makes residuals normally distributed and stabilizes error variance; predictions must be explicitly inversed via expm1 before scoring.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to apply np.expm1 on test predictions before saving submission.csv.

when_to_use: Foundational baseline for image classification/regression tasks using established backbones (e.g. convnext_small, efficientnet_b2, resnet50).
tradeoffs: Leverages ImageNet pretraining weights for rapid convergence with few data; high GPU memory usage for large backbones.
common_pitfalls: Hardcoding input image size to 224x224 when specific backbones expect different resolutions in timm default_cfg.

when_to_use: Regularizing vision models and increasing effective sample size on all image training sets.
tradeoffs: Prevents memorization of spatial artifacts; aggressive augmentation can corrupt fine-grained visual labels.
common_pitfalls: Applying non-deterministic augmentations (e.g. flips, crops) to validation/test sets instead of strictly train folds.

when_to_use: Training deep vision architectures on medium-to-large datasets to improve out-of-distribution robustness and calibration.
tradeoffs: Significantly smooths decision boundaries and prevents overconfidence; requires soft target cross-entropy loss.
common_pitfalls: Applying Mixup to one-hot hard labels without computing linear combination of loss across both target classes.

when_to_use: Inference-stage ensemble boosting by averaging predictions of original image and slightly augmented views (horizontal flip, multi-scale).
tradeoffs: Consistently yields 0.3%-1% metric improvement with zero retraining; multiplies inference time by number of TTA passes.
common_pitfalls: Using non-invariant augmentations during TTA (e.g. vertical flips on tasks with gravity-aligned objects like cars/buildings).

when_to_use: Datasets where raw images have non-square aspect ratios or high-resolution details.
tradeoffs: Resize with padding (letterbox) preserves aspect ratio without distortion; naive squishing distorts visual features.
common_pitfalls: Squishing non-square images into a square matrix, distorting shapes of objects critical for classification.

technique_name: Weighted Random Sampler for Class Imbalance
when_to_use: Severe class imbalance in CV classification tasks where minority classes appear infrequently.
tradeoffs: Ensures mini-batches have balanced representation of rare classes; frequent sampling of minority instances can overfit rare examples.
common_pitfalls: Using replacement=False on WeightedRandomSampler when drawing more samples than the minority class count.
related_techniques: Focal Loss for Extreme Class Imbalance

technique_name: Learning Rate Warmup and Cosine Annealing
when_to_use: Fine-tuning pretrained vision backbones to avoid disrupting pretrained weights in early epochs.
tradeoffs: Smooth convergence and superior final minima; requires configuring total epoch count in scheduler beforehand.
common_pitfalls: Stepping the scheduler per epoch instead of per optimizer step when using cosine with warmup.

when_to_use: Fine-tuning deep pretrained backbones: applying smaller LR to early feature extractors and higher LR to newly initialized classification heads.
tradeoffs: Preserves general low-level vision filters while adapting high-level heads quickly; requires parameter grouping in optimizer.
common_pitfalls: Applying high learning rates to early layers, destroying pretrained ImageNet weights in the first few iterations.
related_techniques: Learning Rate Warmup and Cosine Annealing

when_to_use: Resource-constrained environments or tiny datasets (<500 images) where full backpropagation would rapidly overfit.
tradeoffs: Freezing backbone saves VRAM and trains in seconds; full fine-tuning achieves higher ceiling when compute permits.
common_pitfalls: Keeping BatchNorm in training mode when backbone weights are frozen, corrupting running statistics.

when_to_use: High-accuracy evaluation on complex scenes by cropping corners and center (FiveCrop/TenCrop).
tradeoffs: Boosts robustness against localized spatial cues; increases validation runtime 5x-10x.
common_pitfalls: Not reshaping batch dimensions correctly before passing multi-crop batches through the model.

when_to_use: Semi-supervised boosting when a large test set is available and model predictions exhibit high confidence (>0.95).
tradeoffs: Expands training distribution; risk of confirmation bias if incorrect high-confidence predictions are reinforced.
common_pitfalls: Including low-confidence pseudo-labels which pollutes training data with false supervision.

technique_name: Model Ensembling Across Diverse Backbones (ConvNet + ViT)
when_to_use: Final model submission combining CNN-based architectures (e.g. ConvNeXt) with self-attention architectures (e.g. Swin / EVA-02).
tradeoffs: Different inductive biases yield orthogonal error distributions and maximal ensemble gain; requires training multiple models.
common_pitfalls: Ensembling near-identical architectures (e.g. ResNet50 and ResNet101) which yields minimal diversity gain.

when_to_use: Image datasets containing multiple captures of the same physical entity (patient X-rays, drone passes over same field).
tradeoffs: Essential for realistic validation; failure to do this causes catastrophic leaderboard drop.
common_pitfalls: Splitting images at the row level when a patient_id column exists, allowing the network to memorize patient appearance.

when_to_use: Preventing overconfidence and calibrating probabilities on noisy or ambiguous image labels.
tradeoffs: Improves generalization and downstream ensemble calibration; slight reduction in peak training accuracy.
common_pitfalls: Setting smoothing parameter too high (>0.2), which degrades class discriminability.
related_techniques: Focal Loss for Extreme Class Imbalance

technique_name: Gradient Accumulation for Large Batch Sizes
when_to_use: Training memory-heavy vision models on limited GPU VRAM where batch_size=32 would cause Out-Of-Memory (OOM).
tradeoffs: Simulates arbitrarily large effective batch sizes with zero additional VRAM; slightly slower execution than pure GPU parallelism.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to zero gradients after every N accumulation steps or dividing loss incorrectly.

when_to_use: Standard acceleration on modern NVIDIA GPUs for 2x-3x faster training and 50% lower VRAM usage.
tradeoffs: Minimal to zero loss in numerical precision; requires GradScaler for fp16 to prevent gradient underflow.
common_pitfalls: Not wrapping the forward pass inside torch.autocast and omitting scaler.step(optimizer).

when_to_use: Averaging weights along the trajectory of SGD/Adam at the end of training to find wider, flatter minima.
tradeoffs: Improves generalization with zero extra inference cost; requires updating BatchNorm statistics before evaluation.
common_pitfalls: Evaluating the SWA model without calling torch.optim.swa_utils.update_bn on training data.
related_techniques: Learning Rate Warmup and Cosine Annealing

when_to_use: Computer vision tasks where each image can possess zero, one, or multiple simultaneous tags/attributes.
tradeoffs: Independent sigmoid activations per class; requires per-class decision threshold tuning instead of argmax.
common_pitfalls: Using CrossEntropyLoss (Softmax) on multi-label tasks, which forces probabilities to sum to 1.0.
related_techniques: Focal Loss for Extreme Class Imbalance

technique_name: Focal Loss for Extreme Class Imbalance
when_to_use: Imbalanced object or anomaly detection where easy negative background examples dominate the gradient.
tradeoffs: Focuses gradient updates on hard, ambiguous examples; adds hyperparameter gamma to tune.
common_pitfalls: Applying high gamma on datasets with label noise, causing the model to overfit mislabeled errors.

when_to_use: Training initial epochs at smaller resolutions (e.g. 160x160) then fine-tuning on higher resolution (e.g. 256x256 or 384x384).
tradeoffs: Saves 60% of total training time while boosting high-resolution accuracy; requires rebuilding dataloader transforms.
common_pitfalls: Not resetting or adjusting the learning rate when stepping up resolution.

when_to_use: State-of-the-art starting baseline for text classification, sentiment, entailment, and regression.
tradeoffs: Unmatched semantic comprehension; high compute cost and VRAM usage relative to GBDT/TF-IDF.
common_pitfalls: Using standard BERT instead of DeBERTa-v3 or RoBERTa which consistently outperform original BERT.

technique_name: Sequence Length Truncation Strategy (Head-Tail vs Max Length)
when_to_use: Long-form documents exceeding 512 tokens where standard truncation loses critical concluding information.
tradeoffs: Concatenating first 256 and last 256 tokens retains introduction and conclusion; middle text is omitted.
common_pitfalls: Default tail-truncation silently throwing away the conclusion or final score of an essay/review.

when_to_use: Specialized texts (medical, biomedical, legal, financial, scientific code).
tradeoffs: Pre-trained tokenizer already understands specialized terminology; slightly more limited checkpoint choices.
common_pitfalls: Fine-tuning standard general English BERT on complex clinical or financial jargon without checking domain checkpoints.

when_to_use: Ensuring leak-free validation and generating out-of-fold probability predictions for stacking/ensembling in NLP.
tradeoffs: Requires training K full transformers; ensures reliable validation scores.
common_pitfalls: Fitting tokenizers or vocabulary sets across all folds simultaneously instead of fold-safe.

technique_name: Mean / Attention Pooling Over Transformer Hidden States
when_to_use: Extracting text representations across full sequences instead of relying exclusively on the [CLS] token vector.
tradeoffs: Mean pooling over attention-masked tokens consistently outperforms [CLS] on sentence embedding and classification tasks.
common_pitfalls: Taking torch.mean over padding tokens without applying attention_mask to zero out padded tokens.

when_to_use: Fine-tuning deep transformers by scaling down learning rate by factor (e.g. 0.9) per layer from top to bottom.
tradeoffs: Preserves core linguistic representations in early layers while aggressively adapting top task-specific heads.
common_pitfalls: Applying a single uniform learning rate across all 12/24 layers which risks catastrophic forgetting.

when_to_use: Fast iteration, small training budgets, or tiny datasets (<1000 examples) to prevent overfitting.
tradeoffs: Reduces backpropagation compute time and VRAM by 40-60%; slightly lowers asymptotic performance ceiling.
common_pitfalls: Leaving all parameters unfrozen when dataset is tiny (<500 examples), leading to immediate overfit.

when_to_use: Extracting dense semantic text embeddings (e.g. BAAI/bge-small-en or all-MiniLM-L6-v2) to pass into LightGBM alongside tabular columns.
tradeoffs: Zero deep learning training required in main pipeline; fast inference; captures global semantics without transformer fine-tuning.
common_pitfalls: Passing high-dimensional raw embeddings (1024-dim) into GBDT without dimensionality reduction or feature selection.

when_to_use: Quick, robust initial NLP baseline that runs in seconds on CPU and provides competitive feature baseline.
tradeoffs: Fast, interpretable n-gram signals; lacks contextual sentence understanding compared to transformers.
common_pitfalls: Setting max_features too high (>50,000) leading to sparse matrix memory overhead in tree training.

when_to_use: Replacing final dropout layer before linear classification head with multiple dropout masks and averaging their outputs.
tradeoffs: Accelerates training convergence and acts as an internal ensemble regularizer with negligible compute overhead.
common_pitfalls: Applying multi-sample dropout to hidden layers instead of the task classification head.

technique_name: Class Imbalance in Text (Class-Weighted Loss & Focal Loss)
when_to_use: Classification tasks where rare classes represent <5% of total corpus examples.
tradeoffs: Forces loss optimization to prioritize difficult minority categories; can increase false positives on rare classes.
common_pitfalls: Evaluating solely on Accuracy rather than Macro-F1 or Balanced Accuracy on imbalanced text.

technique_name: Multi-Label Text Classification with Per-Class Thresholds
when_to_use: Documents categorized under multiple non-mutually exclusive topic tags.
tradeoffs: Optimizing individual class thresholds on validation OOF predictions yields 2-5% F1 gain over fixed 0.5 threshold.
common_pitfalls: Defaulting to threshold=0.5 for all classes regardless of class prior frequency.

when_to_use: Pre-processing raw user-generated text containing HTML entities, unicode artifacts, and inconsistent whitespace.
tradeoffs: Standardizes tokenization inputs; destructive cleaning (e.g. stripping punctuation/casing) can destroy capitalization emphasis signal.
common_pitfalls: Aggressively lowercasing text when using a cased transformer checkpoint (e.g. bert-base-cased).

technique_name: Pseudo-Labeling with Semi-Supervised Learning in NLP
when_to_use: Large unlabelled test set where confident predictions are added back into the training corpus for an extra epoch.
tradeoffs: Adapts model to test domain vocabulary; sensitive to threshold selection.
common_pitfalls: Re-training without warm starting or learning rate adjustment, causing instability.

when_to_use: Combining predictions from distinct transformer families (DeBERTa-v3 + RoBERTa + Electra).
tradeoffs: High diversity boost on competition leaderboards; requires managing multiple tokenizer pipelines.
common_pitfalls: Averaging raw uncalibrated logits across models instead of probabilities or rank-normalized scores.

technique_name: Gradient Checkpointing for Long Sequence Memory Optimization
when_to_use: Enabling longer sequence lengths (e.g. 1024 or 2048) on limited GPU memory by recomputing activations during backward pass.
tradeoffs: Reduces peak VRAM by up to 60%; increases training time by approximately 20%.
common_pitfalls: Enabling checkpointing when batch size is already small enough to fit in VRAM, causing unnecessary slowdown.

technique_name: Weight Decay and AdamW Optimizer Configuration
when_to_use: Standard optimizer for transformer fine-tuning with weight decay decoupled from L2 norm.
tradeoffs: Crucial for preventing transformer overfit; requires excluding bias and LayerNorm parameters from weight decay.
common_pitfalls: Applying weight decay to bias and LayerNorm.weight parameters.

when_to_use: Datasets where multiple reviews, tweets, or sentences belong to the same author or source document.
tradeoffs: Ensures model learns generalizable patterns rather than memorizing author writing style; reduces available training independence.
common_pitfalls: Splitting randomly across sentences from the same paragraph or document, leading to severe test score drops.

technique_name: Cross-Encoder Re-ranking for Pairwise Text Matching
when_to_use: Tasks requiring similarity scoring, question-answering matching, or duplicate text detection.
tradeoffs: Full cross-attention between text pairs yields highest possible matching accuracy; slower inference than bi-encoders.
common_pitfalls: Encoding texts separately with a Bi-Encoder and computing cosine similarity when accuracy on complex relationships is required.

when_to_use: Adding small norm-bounded adversarial perturbations to word embeddings during backpropagation to improve generalization.
tradeoffs: Consistently yields 0.3-0.8% CV improvement on competitive NLP tasks; increases training step duration by 2x.
common_pitfalls: Setting perturbation epsilon too high, corrupting the semantic embedding space.

when_to_use: Converting raw 1D audio waveforms into 2D time-frequency representations for vision-like CNN processing.
tradeoffs: Standard, robust representation aligned with human auditory perception; discards phase information.
common_pitfalls: Omitting librosa.power_to_db (log scaling), leaving spectrograms in linear amplitude where signals are crushed.

when_to_use: State-of-the-art transfer learning for environmental audio and sound classification using self-attention over spectrogram patches.
tradeoffs: High accuracy on standard audio benchmarks; computationally heavy during training.
common_pitfalls: Extracting spectrograms with different hop_length or n_mels than AST's expected input dimensions.

when_to_use: Fast, highly robust convolutional audio feature extractor pretrained on AudioSet.
tradeoffs: Excellent generalization across wide sound categories; faster inference and lower VRAM than AST.
common_pitfalls: Not normalizing audio sample rate to 32kHz (AudioSet standard) before passing to PANNs models.

when_to_use: Zero-cost data augmentation directly on spectrograms by zeroing out random horizontal (frequency) and vertical (time) strips.
tradeoffs: Forces the network to be invariant to partial frequency loss and temporal dropouts; essential for preventing spectrogram overfit.
common_pitfalls: Masking too large a fraction of the time or frequency channels, removing the actual acoustic event.

when_to_use: Handling variable-length audio clips into uniform tensor shapes for batched GPU processing.
tradeoffs: Enables vectorized mini-batching; random crop during training acts as data augmentation while center crop ensures deterministic validation.
common_pitfalls: Zero-padding short clips at the end without repeating or looping, creating massive silent blocks.

when_to_use: Pre-processing pipeline requirement: ensuring every audio file is resampled to a consistent target rate (e.g. 16kHz or 32kHz).
tradeoffs: Critical for comparable feature extraction; high quality resampling (torchaudio.transforms.Resample) should happen once offline.
common_pitfalls: Feeding mixed-sample-rate audio files into the same feature extractor, distorting frequency scales across examples.

technique_name: Group K-Fold on Speaker / Environment ID
when_to_use: Whenever multiple audio recordings come from the same speaker, microphone, or recording location.
tradeoffs: Guarantees generalization to unseen speakers/rooms; without it, model memorizes background acoustics.
common_pitfalls: Random row splitting which allows the model to achieve 99% CV by recognizing acoustic background hum.

when_to_use: Compact acoustic representation (13-40 coefficients) for speech recognition, speaker ID, or lightweight GBDT audio models.
tradeoffs: Low dimensional, decorrelated features suitable for classical ML; discards fine-grained acoustic textures.
common_pitfalls: Using standard MFCCs for environmental bird/animal sound classification where higher-order spectral details matter.

when_to_use: Musical instrument recognition and pitch detection where frequency bins should be geometrically spaced per musical octave.
tradeoffs: Matches musical pitch intervals; computationally slower than standard Fast Fourier Transform (FFT).
common_pitfalls: Using standard linear STFT for polyphonic music tasks where octave relationships are logarithmic.

when_to_use: Noisy bioacoustic environments (e.g. rainforest, outdoor sensors) with dynamic background noise floors.
tradeoffs: Performs temporal automatic gain control and dynamic range compression; superior to log-mel in changing acoustic noise.
common_pitfalls: Tuning PCEN parameters without validating on out-of-fold validation set.

when_to_use: Raw waveform augmentation to introduce variance in temporal position and slight acoustic pitch.
tradeoffs: Increases model invariance to pitch variance and onset timing; excessive pitch shift can alter species/voice identity.
common_pitfalls: Applying large pitch shifts on pitch-critical audio tasks (e.g. musical pitch classification).

when_to_use: Injecting white/pink noise or ambient acoustic tracks at varying SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratios).
tradeoffs: Substantially improves model robustness to real-world noisy test sets; can overpower subtle audio signals if SNR is too low.
common_pitfalls: Adding noise with high amplitude that completely masks faint target acoustic signals.

when_to_use: Input preprocessing when dataset contains inconsistent audio channels (mixture of 1-channel mono and 2-channel stereo).
tradeoffs: Standardizes tensor input to single channel; simple average across channels (torch.mean(audio, dim=0, keepdim=True)).
common_pitfalls: Passing multi-channel audio directly into mono-expecting spectrogram extractors without downmixing first.

when_to_use: Combining attention-based Audio Spectrogram Transformer with convolutional CNN14 predictions.
tradeoffs: Combines global attention with localized convolutional pattern recognition; yields significant leaderboard boost.
common_pitfalls: Averaging raw unnormalized logits from different architectures instead of applying sigmoid/softmax probabilities first.

technique_name: Class Imbalance in Audio Events (Threshold Tuning & Pos-Weight)
when_to_use: Rare acoustic event detection where target sounds occur in <2% of recordings.
tradeoffs: Setting pos_weight in BCEWithLogitsLoss penalizes missed acoustic events; requires post-processing threshold tuning.
common_pitfalls: Using default 0.5 probability threshold for rare sound events.

technique_name: Audio Mixup Augmentation on Waveforms and Spectrograms
when_to_use: Acoustic modeling where linear superposition of sound waves reflects physical reality.
tradeoffs: Physically realistic data augmentation for audio; requires training with linear combination of soft labels.
common_pitfalls: Applying mixup without updating the multi-label target vectors proportionally.

technique_name: Weakly Supervised Audio Tagging with Attention Pooling
when_to_use: Recordings labeled at clip level without timestamp annotations of where the sound event occurs.
tradeoffs: Learns to focus on salient temporal acoustic frames and aggregates predictions across time; superior to mean/max pooling.
common_pitfalls: Using simple average pooling across long 60-second clips, which dilutes a 1-second sound event to zero.

when_to_use: Speech recognition, speaker transcription, or linguistic audio classification tasks.
tradeoffs: Processes raw 1D audio directly without handcrafted spectrograms; large model footprints and VRAM requirements.
common_pitfalls: Fine-tuning Whisper/wav2vec on non-speech acoustic audio (e.g. engine noise) where spectrogram models perform better.

technique_name: Silence Removal and Voice Activity Detection (VAD)
when_to_use: Audio recordings with prolonged dead silence before or after the event of interest.
tradeoffs: Eliminates uninformative quiet periods; prevents wasting model capacity on ambient room silence.
common_pitfalls: Setting energy threshold too high and trimming out the soft tail or onset of quiet sounds.

technique_name: Test-Time Augmentation on Audio (Time-Shift & Multi-Window TTA)
when_to_use: Inference-time ensemble on audio by averaging predictions from multiple overlapping sliding windows.
tradeoffs: Reduces edge boundary cutoff errors during evaluation; increases inference time linearly with window count.
common_pitfalls: Averaging sliding window predictions on variable-length audio without weighting by window coverage.
